notes.title: LEFT ALIVE Version 1.03
notes.content:
■Update History
・Version 1.03

Update Contents
■ Bug fixes
・Fixed an issue that caused crashes under certain circumstances in the Steam version.
 
■ Difficulty level adjustments
▼Updates to all difficulty levels
・Added 2 First Aid Kits to each main character's starting equipment.
・Increased the amount of each main character's starting ammo.
　-Additionally, changed the number of bullets lost in the encounter with the ally soldier in Chapter 01 from "all" to "eight."

・Reduced enemy accuracy.

・Reduced damage dealt to players by frag grenades.

・Added a new difficulty level and changed the wording of the "Survivor" achievement.
Previous text: Finished the game on Light or Standard difficulty.
Updated text: Finished the game for the first time.

▼New Difficulty Level: CASUAL
・You can now play on a new difficulty level called CASUAL.
　This mode is for those wanting to go in guns blazing.
　It is a level below LIGHT.
-------------------------------------------------------------
・Increases your attack strength and heavily reduces the damage you take
・Increases your ammo limit
・Heavily reduces enemy health
・Increases damage dealt by headshots and attacks from behind, making it possible for one blow to deal heavy damage
・Increases durability of the Wanzers you pilot
-------------------------------------------------------------
You can start a new file with these updates by selecting NEW GAME from the title screen.
You can change the difficulty level of your current save file in the in-game OPTIONS menu.

notes.title: Left Alive review - a maddeningly messy mech/stealth hybrid
notes.content:
Left Alive is the second new release this week that reminds me of a PS2 game, although perhaps the comparisons this time around aren't so favourable. Devil May Cry 5 is a full-blooded return that reimagines Capcom's action formula and delivers it with the muscle and aplomb of the current generation. Left Alive, meanwhile, takes some fairly rusty, more contemporary mechanics and smothers them in the janky wrappings of a mid-tier PS2 game. It's a flaky, barely functioning stealth game that's almost entirely awful. I kind of love it.

Maybe that's because the promise of its set-up still manages to occasionally shine through the grot. This is ostensibly a spin-off of Square Enix's Front Mission, the mech-infused strategy series whose last entry was another spin-off - Double Helix's third-person shooter Front Mission Evolved - some nine years ago. It's helmed by a veteran producer of FromSoft's Armored Core games - another mech series that's been missing in action - though surprisingly given the expertise on tap, as well as the thirst for a decent mech game, the machines remain mostly in the background.

Instead, this is primarily a survival-infused stealth game - think Metal Gear Survive without that game's strong foundations, with a clunky, unreliable moveset and AI adversaries who aren't undead but don't seem to act on any human impulses, and who are either blindly ignorant or supernaturally aware of your presence depending on their own whims. It's bizarre how much Left Alive wants to be Metal Gear Solid; there are fudgy treatise on the human cost of war and hard to follow strands of conspiracy theories while familiar audio and visual cues have been seemingly lifted and clumsily pasted over the action.

notes.title: Left Alive is out now but may be best left alone
notes.content:
Left Alive – Square Enix’s stealthy reboot of the Front Mission mech-tactics series – is out now, but word on the information super-street is that it never should have been cleared for deployment. It’s not a huge shock, as footage released a couple weeks back looked very stiff, and its branching dialogues felt stilted. Worst sin of all was that the mech-on-mech battles just looked awkward and flailing. A shame, considering this had some noted talent involved, including a director from the Armored Core series, and Metal Gear’s character artist. There’s a launch trailer for the curious below, plus an alternative recommendation.

notes.title: Left Alive looks more Alpha Protocol than Metal Gear
notes.content:
Despite being set in the same universe as Square Enix’s old Front Mission strategy series, Left Alive is ostensibly more of a Metal Gear-styled stealth game with the occasional mech fight. At least, that’s the plan, but for better or worse, today’s fourteen minutes of new footage reminds me most of Alpha Protocol, Obsidian’s endearingly janky spy RPG. See what you make of its slightly offbeat blend of stealth, branching dialogues, equipment crafting and even a little bit of mech combat in the video below. The game launches on March 5th, just ten days from now.

notes.title: Left Alive s latest trailer is an oddly vague reintroduction to the world of Front Mission
notes.content:
If today’s trailer for sci-fi tactical shooter (with mecha bits) Left Alive is any indication, Front Mission’s awkward relationship with the PC might not be changing. The Tokyo Game Show trailer gives us a frustratingly vague (if pretty) glimpse at the war-torn future nation of Novo Slava and the characters players will be sneaking around it as. What it doesn’t feature in great quantity is mech battles, despite Left Alive being set in Square Enix’s long-running Front Mission universe. Below: Not the robots you’re looking for.

notes.content:
Last week we released both a teaser and a full trailer for Left Alive and today I'm here to give you a quick recap of what was shown off!

Then on Thursday (21st) during TGS we released an announcement trailer, which features a first look at one of the characters in the game, as well as a very quick flash of gameplay towards the end of the video. Finally, we've also started both [url=twitter.com/leftalivegame.com]Twitter[/url] and [url=facebook.com/leftalivegame.com]Facebook[/url] accounts for Left Alive! (@LeftAliveGame on both)

Make sure you're following both to keep up to date with everything to do with Left Alive, and don't forget it's out on Steam in 2018. What do you think of what we've shown off so far? Comment below or let us know using the hashtag #LeftAlive

notes.title: Square Enix announce mech game Left Alive
notes.content: You can learn a lot about someone from their response to a Christmas disaster. When tragedy struck snowy New York in Tom Clancy’s The Division, Ubisoft activated sleeper agents to shoot bad men. A trite and telling reaction. When Mr. Bean got his head stuck in the Christmas turkey, he wrapped a towel round it so his girlfriend wouldn’t find out. That’s classic Bean. When a city goes to heck in Left Alive [official site], Square Enix send in mechs. Heck yes! Announced today, Left Alive is mysterious a “survival action shooter” coming in 2018. Observe: (more…)
